title: Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals Introduce VULCAN Hybrid Framework for Scalable Quantum Chemistry - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals introduce VULCAN, a hybrid quantum-classical chemistry framework that replaces ADAPT-VQE's gradient-measurement screening with gradient-free layered growth, overlap compression, subspace projection and GPU perturbation theory, reaching chemical accuracy at 5-20% of batched ADAPT-VQE measurement cost and converging on 32-qubit C3H6 where ADAPT-VQE stalls; a proof-of-principle ran on Quantinuum's H2.

insights.claim: VULCAN, a hybrid quantum-classical electronic-structure framework from Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals, is designed to eliminate the Hamiltonian gradient-measurement bottleneck of adaptive variational quantum eigensolvers (ADAPT-VQE).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Measurement cost is the main practical barrier to quantum chemistry on NISQ hardware; cutting it improves commercial viability for drug-discovery players.

insights.claim: Instead of screening thousands of candidate operators via energy gradients each iteration, VULCAN derives relevant excitations in seconds from a one-body Variational Double Bracket Flow commutator with the molecular Hamiltonian, completes them into a linearly scaling Minimal Complete Pool, and appends full layers at once.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gradient-free pool generation shifts work from expensive quantum measurements to cheap classical computation.
insights.locator: Rather than screening thousands of candidate operators

insights.claim: VULCAN's operator pools are 4x-25x smaller than QEB pools, e.g. 1,480 versus 36,456 operators on 32-qubit C3H6.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Smaller pools mean fewer measurements and shorter runtimes on scarce quantum hardware.

insights.claim: VULCAN's overlap-guided compression ranks operators by single-measurement state-overlap gradients and cut CNOT counts below batched ADAPT-VQE on 4 of 7 benchmarks, reaching 0.14x baseline CNOTs on stretched H10.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shallower circuits are more tolerant of NISQ noise, widening the set of molecules runnable today.

insights.claim: Projecting the Hamiltonian onto 2k dominant determinants reduces required qubits by 23%-50% (e.g. 26 to 20 qubits on H2O) and Pauli terms by 60%-88%, with 40%-74% fewer CNOTs after basis optimization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Qubit-count reduction lets chemistry problems fit on smaller current machines.

themes.theme: Benchmark results and classical GPU offload

insights.claim: In GPU-accelerated statevector benchmarks up to 32 qubits, VULCAN reached chemical accuracy at 5% to 20% of the measurement cost of batched ADAPT-VQE across hydrogen chains, BeH2 and H2O.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 5-20x measurement-cost reduction is a direct cost lever for cloud quantum chemistry workloads.

insights.claim: Pairing a single quantum layer with GPU-based stochastic Epstein-Nesbet second-order perturbation theory let VULCAN reach chemical accuracy on 32-qubit C3H6 (1.0e-3 Ha error) and 26-qubit H2O (0.05% of baseline measurements) where batched ADAPT-VQE failed to converge.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Offloading correlation energy to classical GPUs enables early VQE termination, a hybrid pattern that boosts GPU vendors' role in quantum workflows.

insights.claim: An initial proof-of-principle run of VULCAN on a Quantinuum System Model H2 trapped-ion processor measured the ground-state energy of molecular hydrogen within 1.7e-3 Ha of the exact reference.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Only a toy-molecule hardware demo so far; watch for larger-molecule hardware runs before treating it as commercially material.
insights.locator: The authors also reported an initial proof-of-principle
